text:
Iris: quick idea — instead of an all-or-nothing pool spillover we use a per-tenant leaky-bucket of spill credits plus jittered migration windows. goal: reduce synchronized migrations and give noisy tenants a backpressure path.

Tom: leaky-bucket meaning credits refill at steady rate and drain on each migration? how do we avoid slow refill starving bursting tenants?

Iris: yes. credits refill proportional to the tenant's soft-reservation and weighted by tenant priority. bursts allowed up to a burst_cap. if bucket empty, migrations are delayed but we surface a graceful fallback (probabilistic admission to fallback pool).

Diego: sounds good. propose adding jitter to migration window start times per-tenant and exponential backoff on repeated rejections to break sync. also track last_migration_ts per-tenant.

Iris: agreed. minimal config sketch:
```yaml
spill_policy:
  refill_interval: 10s
  refill_per_interval: 1
  burst_cap_multiplier: 3.0
  per_tier:
    enterprise:
      refill_per_interval: 4
      burst_cap_multiplier: 5.0
    standard:
      refill_per_interval: 1
      burst_cap_multiplier: 2.0
  migration_window:
    base: 4s
    jitter: 0.0-2.5s
  backoff:
    initial: 2s
    factor: 2.0
    max: 120s
  scoring_weight:
    latency_impact: 0.6
    cost_impact: 0.4
```

Tom: +1. A few tradeoffs: 1) refill rate tuning is critical — too high and we negate isolation, too low and bursty tenants suffer. 2) jitter prevents thundering herd but complicates observability.

Diego: on observability: emit per-tenant metric streams: credit_level, migrations_attempted, migrations_success, last_backoff. aggregate to pool-level for alerts.

Iris: also propose a small fast-path for p99-sensitive routes: mark route "critical" and allow single credit overdraft (audit log + tagged metric) to avoid user-impacting latency. overdraft still subject to backoff if abused.

Tom: operator controls: emergency_drain command that forces migrations ignoring buckets (requires approval and logs). Also a read-only diagnostic endpoint that simulates refill curves given a tenant's history.

Diego: testing plan: unit tests for refill math and backoff; load tests with 200 tenants where 20% spike to 8x concurrently; verify migrations_continuous_rate <= 2x baseline and p99 uplift < 15% for critical routes.

Iris: failure modes: if operator misconfigures burst_cap_multiplier too high, we lose isolation. add conservative defaults and a safety circuit: global_pool_overcommit_threshold -> open circuit that pauses new migrations until operator clears.

infra-bot: feature-flag rollout started: "spill_leaky_bucket_v1" enabled in eu-central at 2961234500. canary shard: shard-7.

pagerbot: suggested alert: "spill_credit_depletion" if percent_tenants_below_threshold > 30% for 5m (P3).

Tom: one more thought — tie refill to actual usage patterns: if tenant consistently underuses reservation, reduce refill; if steady near reservation, keep refill. avoids rewarding spiky tenants with persistent credits.

Iris: good idea. include an adaptive-refill_mode: {fixed, usage_based}. Default fixed for now; plan to evaluate usage_based in later iteration.

Diego: put RFC draft in #docs once you have math and experiments. I'll add a chaos test harness for simulated jitter and backoff.

Iris: will open RFC. thanks team.

pagerbot: note: ensure audit log entry for every emergency_drain invocation (user, reason, timestamp).

Tom: assigning follow-ups: Iris -> RFC + cost model; Diego -> chaos harness; Tom -> dashboard panels & alerts.

Iris: wrapping up here. will post RFC link when ready.
